\section[il rischio]{il rischio — the risk}

\label{lesson:IT-C376-rischio}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for final, then the Italian for to fix.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: il rischio}
\textbf{il rischio} — \textquotedblleft{}the risk\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Se non prenoti, corri il rischio di non trovare posto.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{If you do not book, you run the risk of not finding a seat.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Correre il rischio} — to run the risk. \emph{A rischio} — at risk.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{rischio} is usually traced to Medieval Latin \emph{risicum}, \emph{resicum}, a word of sea trade. The deeper origin is not settled: EtymDB gives no source for \emph{rischio} (EtymDB), and Greek and Arabic sources have both been proposed.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{il rischio}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{il rischio}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Italian for final, then the Italian for to fix, then say \emph{il rischio} again
\end{itemize}

\section[rischioso]{rischioso — risky}

\label{lesson:IT-C376-rischioso}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for to fix, then the Italian for the risk.

\subsection*{You'll want to know: rischioso}
\textbf{rischioso} — \textquotedblleft{}risky\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Guidare con la nebbia è rischioso.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Driving in fog is risky.}
\end{quote}

Built on \emph{rischio}. \emph{Rischiare} is the verb.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{rischioso} is built on \emph{rischio} \textquotedblleft{}risk\textquotedblright{}, usually traced to Medieval Latin \emph{risicum}, a word whose deeper origin is not settled; EtymDB lists \emph{rischio} without a source (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.

\section[probabile]{probabile — likely, probable}

\label{lesson:IT-C376-probabile}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for the risk, then the Italian for risky.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: probabile}
\textbf{probabile} — \textquotedblleft{}likely, probable\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
È probabile che arrivi più tardi.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{It is likely that he will arrive later.}
\end{quote}

\emph{È probabile che} takes the subjunctive. \emph{Probabilmente} — probably.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{probabile} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{probābilis} \textquotedblleft{}that may be proved, credible\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short), from \emph{probāre} \textquotedblleft{}to test, to approve\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{probabile}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{probabile}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Italian for the risk, then the Italian for risky, then say \emph{probabile} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[improbabile]{improbabile — unlikely}

\label{lesson:IT-C376-improbabile}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for risky, then the Italian for likely.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: improbabile}
\textbf{improbabile} — \textquotedblleft{}unlikely\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
È improbabile che nevichi a maggio.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{It is unlikely to snow in May.}
\end{quote}

Also takes the subjunctive after \emph{è improbabile che}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{improbabile} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{improbābilis} \textquotedblleft{}not deserving approval\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short), from \emph{in-} \textquotedblleft{}not\textquotedblright{} and \emph{probābilis}; the sense \textquotedblleft{}unlikely\textquotedblright{} follows \emph{probabile}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[la probabilità]{la probabilità — the probability, the chance}

\label{lesson:IT-C376-probabilita}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for likely, then the Italian for unlikely.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: la probabilità}
\textbf{la probabilità} — \textquotedblleft{}the probability, the chance\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Ci sono poche probabilità di vincere.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{There is little chance of winning.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Con ogni probabilità} — in all likelihood.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{probabilità} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{probābilitās} \textquotedblleft{}likelihood\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short), from \emph{probābilis} \textquotedblleft{}credible\textquotedblright{}, on \emph{probāre} \textquotedblleft{}to test\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
